chapter: Family, Margaret's story and Eutris's memories
title: Garnett's trombone playing and tailor shop
summary: Garnett played as a sideline and ran a tailor shop on Auburn Avenue.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Jay C., you said one time that you had picked up his trombone.
I just picked it up once and played one note and put it down. That was the only time I ever bothered his horn.
But also you said that he had just played it around school; he didn't play it professionally. He didn't ever play any jobs with it, just as a hobby.
The only job that I can remember him playing was out in Decatur. They played in a hall one night. I think that's how he happened to pick up this trombone, he and his friend, Ben (Cofer.)
Who's Ben Cofer?
That was one of my brother's best friends, because they were in business there in Atlanta.
Did they have a band or something?
No, they didn't have a band; they had a tailor shop. My brother, you know, he taught tailoring at Morris Brown, but he also had a tailor shop on Auburn Avenue.
Which brother was that now?
Garnett.
But now you said that he came out to Decatur to play.
Yes, we lived in Decatur.
Yes, right, but what I'm trying to get at is, what band did Garnett come out to play with?
No, it wasn't a band. Just played at this - it was a dance, played for this dance at this hall.
No regular band. He just did it for a sideline.
You know whose band it was?
No, it wasn't a band. I don't think so, because there was only two of them there playing that night with the piano. I don't even remember who was playing the piano.
You see, the point I'm trying to get at is that, we're all musicians and we're trying to pinpoint if there were any influences who inspired him - but you say Garnett was the one.
I'm sure, yes.
Right. You said you were living in Decatur?
